$comment: How body settings translate into per-attribute maximums.
STILL THE WEAKEST FILE IN THE DATASET. The magnitudes below are invented. What IS sourced from
2K27 coverage (2026-08-25) is:
- height, weight and wingspan directly set your max attribute caps;
- body settings matter MUCH more in 2K27 than in previous titles;
- a guard or wing at MINIMUM weight and MINIMUM wingspan takes a significant hit to
PERIMETER DEFENSE and DRIVING DUNK specifically.
That last point corrected two coefficient SIGNS that were wrong in the first draft: perimeter
defense and driving dunk now rise with weight and wingspan rather than falling with them.
Coefficients have also been scaled up to reflect 'much larger impact'.
Model: cap(attr) = round( baseCap
+ perInchHeight    * (height   - refHeight)
+ perPoundWeight   * (weight   - refWeight)
+ perInchWingspan  * (wingspan - refWingspan)
+ positionAdjust[position] )
clamped to [hardMin, hardMax] and to the global rating floor/ceiling.
The `overrides` table takes precedence and lets you ship an exact lookup table instead of a model.
Override keys: `<POSITION>|<heightInches>|<weight>|<wingspanInches>` — partial keys are supported
using `*` for 'any', and the most specific matching key wins. The NBA 2K HQ app's builder is the
right place to read exact caps off and paste them in here.

verification.source: 2K27 builder coverage for the DIRECTION and relative importance of each body effect.
verification.notes: Directions are sourced. Magnitudes are invented, and now MEASURABLY WRONG — see measuredAccuracy. Replace with exact tables in `overrides`.

$comment: Scored against the 35 attribute caps PROVEN across three transcribed builds. Caps are proven by
two routes — a cap breaker ladder ending in a locked slot, and the slider screen's 'current / MAX'
figure — and where both apply they agree exactly (Three-Point 93 on the 6'5" frame).
- mean absolute error 6.3 points; worst is Steal on the 6'11" PF, +16.
- biased HIGH on 24 of 35, so builds planned off the model look more affordable than they are.
- on 7 further attributes the model sat BELOW a proven floor, i.e. it claimed a ceiling the builder
was observed to exceed. computeCaps now lifts those to the floor, so that class of error is gone.
An earlier figure of 12.9 was measured against the WRONG numbers — see meta.json 0.7.0 — and is
withdrawn. The model has still not been refit: three bodies cannot calibrate four coefficients per
attribute, and a model that looks calibrated without being calibrated is worse than an honest one.

verification.notes: Weight and wingspan signs are POSITIVE on the sourced note that minimum weight + minimum wingspan hurts driving dunk.
Weight and wingspan signs are POSITIVE on the sourced note that minimum weight + minimum wingspan hurts perimeter defense.

$comment: Exact caps keyed by `<POSITION>|<height>|<weight>|<wingspan>`; `*` matches anything. Most specific wins.
`caps` are proven ceilings, `capFloors` are proven LOWER BOUNDS (the real cap is at least this, and
computeCaps takes max(modelled, floor) so it can never claim a cap below something known reachable).
`capEvidence` records how each exact cap was established.
TWO ROUTES PROVE A CAP, and they agree where they overlap:
'builder-max'  — the attribute slider screen prints 'current / MAX' beside each attribute. Direct.
'ladder-lock'  — a cap breaker ladder that ends in a LOCKED slot has run into the ceiling, so that
row's New Cap is the cap. A ladder using all five slots without locking merely ran
out of slots and yields a floor only.
Three-Point on the 6'5" frame is 93 by both routes, which is what licenses 'ladder-lock' elsewhere.
WHAT IS NOT A CAP: the builder's attribute page, and the Cap Breaker page's 'Original Cap' column,
both show what the player ALLOCATED. Reading those as ceilings put wrong data in this file once
already — see meta.json 0.7.0.

verification.notes: Two independent derivations, and where they overlap they agree exactly. (1) LADDER-LOCK: a cap breaker ladder that ends in a locked slot has reached this frame's ceiling, so its New Cap is the cap. (2) BUILDER-MAX: the attribute slider screen prints 'current / MAX' beside each attribute. Three-Point on this frame is 93 by both routes. A ladder that spends all five slots without locking ran out of slots rather than reaching the ceiling, so it only yields a lower bound and lives in capFloors.
